observations.boundary: A direct critical comparison, not a claim that the two films have identical plots or politics.

observations.summary: Guest calls the two Karlson Westerns a thematic diptych. Their father-son conflicts join psychological family struggle to vigilantism, placing ordinary men’s private burdens inside an American wartime logic that treats violence as necessary.

observations.boundary: A documented thematic connection within Karlson’s work, not a general claim about all Westerns.

observations.boundary: An oeuvre-level formal comparison, not a claim that the three narratives share the same historical meaning.

observations.boundary: A direct oeuvre comparison; the trilogy label is thematic rather than a serialized narrative claim.

observations.boundary: A curatorial contrast between practices, not a claim that every listed film uses the same formal strategy.

observations.summary: Within Rainer’s work, Lives of Performers, Film About a Woman Who... and Kristina Talking Pictures combine fragmented fiction, autobiography, voiceover and performance, becoming reference points in debates on feminist cinema.

author: Robert Koehler

verification.note: Read the original BFI page; agent review only.

passages.text: The narrative feature film underwent a revision

observations.summary: Koehler situates L’Avventura within a 1959–60 break from closed plots, genre security and privileged psychology. Breathless fractures conventional crime time, Marienbad participates in the new novel’s formal dislocation, and Time Stood Still exemplifies Italy’s move beyond neorealist codes.
observations.summaryKo: 쾰러는 <정사>를 닫힌 결말·장르의 안정·심리 중심 서사에서 벗어난 1959–60년의 전환에 놓는다. <네 멋대로 해라>의 시간 파괴, <마리엔바드에서의 지난해>의 누보로망적 전위, <시간은 멈췄다>의 후기 네오리얼리즘이 이 순간을 구성한다.
observations.boundary: A historical constellation of distinct modernisms, not a claim that the films share one style or direct influence chain.
